body:
`case_study:luckin-coffee-2020` | 2020-04-02 | tickers: US-LKNCY | confidence: verified

Luckin IPO'd on Nasdaq in May 2019 at $17 and peaked ~$50 in Jan 2020. On 31 Jan 2020 Muddy Waters circulated an anonymous 89-page report (based on ~11,000 hours of store video) alleging inflated items-per-order and revenue. On 2 Apr 2020 Luckin admitted COO Jian Liu fabricated ~RMB 2.2 bn ($310 m) of 2019 Q2-Q4 sales; shares fell ~80% in a day; Nasdaq delisted it on 29 Jun 2020; Chapter 15 restructuring 2021; SEC $180 m settlement. Paradox: after a management/ownership change, Luckin grew into China's largest coffee chain by store count and its OTC stock recovered multiples from the 2020 low -- shareholders who bought the fraud peak still lost heavily for years. Visible flags: (1) hyper-growth with deep discounts and losses; (2) chairman Lu Zhengyao and others had pledged most of their shares for margin loans; (3) related-party history (Car Inc/UCAR team); (4) a follow-on offering and convertible raised within months of IPO; (5) the short report's on-the-ground data (independent verification beats reported numbers). Lesson: alt-data/scuttlebutt can refute reported unit economics; founder margin loans are a forced-selling and governance flag. A fraud can sit inside a real business -- the equity outcome depends on entry price and dilution.

**Lesson:** Independent alt-data can falsify reported numbers
**Spotted early by:** Muddy Waters (anonymous report); store-traffic counters
